title: Pentagon releases new UFO files: images of mysterious objects and formations that remained unexplained
excerpt: Pentagon releases new UFO files: images of mysterious objects and formations that remained unexplained
content:
mystery

Express newspaper

22/09/2026 20:39

The Pentagon has released another batch of documents and footage related to unidentified aerial phenomena, including cases recorded decades ago and more recent videos from the Middle East.

The sixth package of materials contains witness reports, videos, declassified documents and data on American programs that have studied advanced technologies and unusual aerial phenomena.

One of the most famous cases in the published documents is a 1952 film, made in Tremonton, Utah, by a US Navy officer.

The famous case of 1952

The images taken by Delbert Newhouse show between 10 and 14 bright objects moving across a clear sky.

Newhouse, who was on vacation with his family at the time, stated that the objects resembled two discs placed one on top of the other, creating the classic shape commonly associated with a "flying saucer."

In incident reports, he described the objects as metallic and shiny, while claiming they moved in a relatively loose formation, heading mainly from the west.

The case was analyzed for months by "Project Blue Book," the US Air Force program that investigated UFO reports during the Cold War.

However, authorities did not reach a definitive explanation for what was filmed.

Unusual formations also over the Middle East

More than 70 years later, US military aircraft have recorded other unusual sights in the Middle East.

One of the videos shows a group of bright objects passing by an oil rig.

The objects appear to move rapidly in a nearly horizontal line and then break up into smaller groups.

The sightings do not determine what the objects are, and the fact that they are classified as unidentified does not mean they are of extraterrestrial origin.

The term UFO, or UAP in newer American terminology, simply refers to a phenomenon that was not identified with certainty at the time of observation.

Millions of dollars for the study of futuristic technologies

The published documents also contain materials related to the AAWSAP program – “Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program”.

The program operated from 2008 to 2012 and funded studies on advanced aeronautical technologies and theoretical concepts that could have military interest.

According to the documents, tens of millions of dollars were spent on research that included advanced materials, directed energy weapons, stealth technology and theoretical concepts for extremely fast space travel.

The idea of ​​"warp drive"

Among the materials are drawings and theoretical analyses for a vehicle that could use the so-called "warp bubble".

In theory, such a system would not propel the ship directly beyond the speed of light.

Instead, the space in front of the vehicle would contract, while that behind it would expand.

In a simpler description, the ship would "travel" within a warp of space-time itself.

This remains a theoretical concept and there is no evidence that such a technology has been practically realized.

Invisibility technology and laser weapons

The documents also address concepts for "cloaking," or hiding objects through the manipulation of light, heat, or radar signals.

The researchers also analyzed laser weapons and other directed energy systems.

Directed energy technologies are already part of modern military research and systems, but that does not mean that the most extreme concepts described in the AAWSAP documents have become reality.

The role of Robert Bigelow's company

The contract for part of this research was awarded to the company Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, or BAASS.

The company was part of the business of Robert Bigelow, the American entrepreneur known for his investments in the space industry and for his long-standing interest in UFOs.

Bigelow has spoken publicly over the years about his interest in unidentified aerial phenomena and the need for greater government transparency on the subject.

In recent months, allegations have also emerged that he may have played a role in political discussions about releasing more information about UFOs.

These claims have not been officially confirmed.

Dozens of new documents are made public

According to the report, a total of 71 files were released in the latest package.

The materials include videos, testimonies, military reports, and documents related to research funded by the US Department of Defense.

Their publication is part of a broader process for declassifying information on unidentified aerial phenomena.

However, no conclusive evidence has been published to date proving that any of the recorded objects are of extraterrestrial origin.

Claims for even more compelling materials in the future

Some UFO researchers, former officials and people who claim to have sources within American institutions say that other materials may be released in the future.

Filmmaker and researcher Mark Christopher Lee has claimed that the releases are being made gradually and that there may be more important documents in the future.

"We are getting more and more evidence that we are not alone," he stated, although this remains a personal view and not a conclusion confirmed by American authorities.

Some religious figures and former military personnel have also claimed that clearer videos or information about so-called "biological materials" could be released.

These claims have not been proven either.

The documents raise questions, but not yet a definitive answer.

The release of the new files is important because it provides more transparency into how the US military and intelligence services have handled reports of unusual objects in the sky.

However, there is a big difference between an unidentified object and a ship of extraterrestrial origin.

So far, the published documents show that the US military has encountered phenomena that in some cases it was unable to immediately identify and that it has funded research into highly advanced technologies.

They do not, however, provide definitive proof that Earth has been visited by extraterrestrial intelligence.

It is precisely this lack of a clear answer that is why the files continue to spark interest, debate, and speculation even decades after some of the most famous cases were recorded. /GazetaExpress/
